PulseChain thesis evidence and authority
30 September 2026. This map separates observed contract state, published source behavior, conditional
arithmetic, scenario assumptions and unresolved execution. It does not identify private-key owners,
certify economic guarantees or authorize any blockchain changes. All new chain requests in this review
are getters, contract-code reads or storage reads.
Reading the evidence
Later evidence in the 1 October Safe/rollup audit (Appendix 52) identifies the Arbitrum timelock and
security-council executor roles and verifies externally owned address control of the UpgradeExecutor and
key bridge proxy admins. Statements below about unresolved role holders describe this older snapshot's
verification status; the later audit supplies the extended authority map without attributing private-key
ownership.
The main observation snapshot is PulseChain block 27,675,130, hash 
0xdd12f23ad571882b63fd333c5d3909a45a05fe6f0a3c2b273cb7e1e6b0917954, at 30 September 2026 05:20:55 UTC.
Separate older observations retain their own block numbers. A contract address observed on PulseChain
refers to that chain, even when the address also exists on Ethereum. Published verified source supports
contract interpretation; this review has not independently compiled all sources and matched every
deployed bytecode dependency.
Raw getter records are in artifacts/pulsechain-deferred-campaign-20260930/ and the new artifacts/pulsechain-
three-round-review-20260930/. Each request records its target, calldata, pinned block and RPC response. The
three new authority manifests are under Research/experiments/ with stems pulsechain_review_authority, 
pulsechain_review_authority_details and pulsechain_review_owner_storage, all dated 20260930. Source
interpretations cite the published SourceCode contents, not imaginary line numbers in JSON.

Rollup owner proxy slots are recorded in owner-storage-rpc.json; the published UpgradeExecutor source is 
rollupOwnerImplementation-source.json in the review batch. Published source for the proxy-admin address
was unavailable. This identifies role requirements without pretending its executor-role holders or
upgrade controller are known.
The executor logic is preserved at artifacts/parb-local-pls-protocol-conditions-20260929/
v3_authority_source.json. Its acceptAdmin checks only the pending caller, while its queue and execution
functions check the current admin, timestamp and queued action. Its minimum delay is 86,400 seconds.
Configurator and ACL sources are configurator_source.json and acl_source.json in that batch. Provider
ownership, ACL grant authority and reserve configuration rights are different checks and have been kept
separate.
Supply headroom at the actual mint
The published validation requires an ordinary supply cap of zero, meaning unlimited, or the integer ray-
math condition:
rayMul(scaledTotalSupply + accruedToTreasury_after_updateState,
       nextLiquidityIndex) + mintAmount <= supplyCap * 10^decimals
Portal separately requires existing unbacked plus new principal to fit its positive unbacked cap. Receipt
burns after a mint do not repair an earlier failed check. Current configuration, index, accrual and
proposed staged allocations must be checked at execution; a snapshot minimum is not a safe permanent
cap recommendation. All seventeen observed reserves were active, unfrozen and unpaused. Source: 
ValidationLogic.validateSupply and BridgeLogic.executeMintUnbacked in the saved pool and linked-library
sources.
Exact examples of token delivery
The documented local route uses pDAI 0x6b175474e89094c44da98b954eedeac495271d0f, V3 aDAI 
0x018008bfb33d285247a21d44e50697654f754e63, waDAI 0x098256c06ab24f5655c5506a6488781bd711c14b and Balancer
linear pool 0x6667c6fa9f2b3fc1cc8d85320b62703d938e4385. Existing local trades do not establish newly delivered
source receipts or current campaign-size funding. Receipt study (Appendix 49).
The historical ARB mint example uses destination ARB 0xb50721bcf8d664c30412cfbc6cf7a15145234ad1, source
counterpart 0x912ce59144191c1204e64559fe8253a0e49e6548 and authorized reverse gateway 
0xbbce8aa77782f13d4202a230d978f361b011db27. This is a token-specific mint, not pDAI issuance or evidence of a
funded ARB-to-pDAI conversion at scale. The examined stablecoin and aT oken router mappings use
escrow routes instead. Gateway inventory (Appendix 4).

Complete route and operating design
These statements belong to the expanded white paper. They do not convert its proposed controller into
deployed behavior or its historical evidence into current operational capacity.

research

overlaps explained. This is bounded

Integrated network extension, 1 October 2026
The integrated network study (Appendix 37) fixes the historical membership cutoff and separates
configured identities, supply behavior and effective control. The new findings do not extend the previous
edition's review approvals to this revision.
Claim Evidence and boundary
P56 Eight historical registry roots yield 618 pools and 381 token
identities at inherited block 17,232,999. Ethereum archive
reads use the verified matching inherited header; 12
underlying-coin reads remain unresolved. This is bounded
registry membership, not current pool funding or every
custom deployment.
P57 A bridge can return an existing L1 pool coin when its L2
address differs. Current DAI/USDC/USDT mappings and
saved exact gateway implementations establish the
identity/release design. Source deployment, authenticated
messages and available escrow remain separate
requirements.
P58 Three sampled configured pairs have identical L1/L2
numeric addresses: PL2, HGOLD and MCB. Current pair
getters plus historical token labels; different chains still
have separate contracts and supply. HGOLD token mint
permissions remain unresolved.
P59 Standard/custom gateways do not generically mint local
stables. Selected current DAI/USDT/OUSD/eUSD/mUSD/
FRAX gateway token balances are zero; USDC has
1,000,000 raw units. Other venues or future deposits may
contribute separately; a failed read is not zero.
P60 FRAX AMOs and DOLA Feds are candidate venue supply
buffers; rebasing tokens and collateral issuance have
distinct mechanisms. Primary architecture descriptions do
not prove installed local controllers, common control or
present capacity.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 172

Claim Evidence and boundary
P61 The sampled OUSD/3CRV account is nonrebasing; the
sampled UZD 0xb40b…9f1c pool is rigid. Current eligibility
getters and inherited/source accounting; other UZD
versions' failed eligibility reads remain unresolved. Pool
accounting needs separate proof before any proposed
rebase integration.
P62 No resolved sampled generic authority comparison differs
from inherited state: 70 matching values, 446 unresolved
records, plus 18 matching controller/storage/delay
comparisons. This neither confirms universal takeover nor
excludes changed voting control. Some new monetary
candidates lack issuer authority reads.
P63 Across HubPool and Safe module owners changed in
verified postfork transactions; current getters agree. T wo
authority changes within Across do not prove UMA
ownership, common private-key ownership or intent to peg
pDAI. Aave's sampled nominee remains pending.
P64 PLS/HEX/PLSX/INC earning positions could contribute
realized support resources. Proposed branch; no generic
Origin/Reserve acceptance of these assets is proved. New
plugins/strategies require compatible authority and
valuation; existing accepted stable collateral is a shorter
alternative.
P65 Connected issuer conversions, supply controllers and
funded venue trades could narrow stablecoin market
differences. Conditional route arithmetic and inventory
accounting; frozen $1 markings do not fund AMM bids, and
relative convergence does not establish external dollar
purchasing power.
P66 Historical final canonical crvUSD address has no code at
the inherited boundary; earlier crvUSD labels remain
unresolved versions. Successful archive code getter, not
inference from later docs. The inherited Mochi USDM
identity is distinct from later Mountain USDM.
Remaining proof requirements
The sUSD extension (Appendix 66) adds P67–P69: six inherited Curve pool connections and sampled
mUSD acceptance (P67); verified copied Synthetix bridge source with messenger/counterpart guards,
enabled transfer setting and the Issuer mapping to the existing sUSD implementation at separate block
27,683,120 (P68); and the distinction between that Optimism-specific issuer path and pARB's zero-
inventory sampled escrow branch (P69). None establishes common governance control, a verified
current source chain or an executed end-to-end transfer.
Its financing extension adds P70–P72: approved collateral wrappers and the explicit historical Optimism
DAI → sUSD → Ethereum bridge/redeem-or-trade precedent in SCCP-264/SCCP-2011 (P70); the version
boundary between later Arbitrum V3 native/spot tokens and inherited PulseChain V2 sUSD (P71); and the
original bridge announcement's seven-day withdrawal wait, equivalent to 60,480 ten-second intervals
(P72). The primary documents and connected metapool rows are frozen in artifacts/pulsechain-susd-
financing-20261001/. Neither upstream proposal status nor timing proves a deployed pARB source,
available copied wrapper capacity, accepted cross-chain messaging or the copied route's delay.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 173

The control and storage audit (Appendix 67) adds P73–P77. The current Synthetix 5-of-13 Safe, Optimism
5-of-7 Safe and nested 2-of-2 Safe retain inherited sampled control values; selected runtime
comparisons match, without proving private-key possession (P73). The copied Optimism fraud-proof
window is 604,800 seconds and its selected postfork state-batch census is empty (P74). The recognized
local DAI/sUSD wrapper has a 20-million-DAI cap, 14.648-million-DAI sampled spare capacity and
unchanged positive fees (P75). Caps, fees and creation of new factory wrappers are owner-controlled
capabilities; authority by the proposed group is unproved (P76). Depositing bought pDAI creates
collateral for eligible synth redemption rather than an exclusive freely spendable treasury reserve or
interest-paying deposit (P77). The exact earlier and later checkpoints, successful selected control census
and collection limitations are preserved separately.
The contract-level proof establishes boundaries and available authority paths. An operational proof still
needs the exact source assets, adapter addresses, destination conversion capacity, funded support
inventory, account execution rights, keeper policy, dollar reference and end-to-end accounting. Outside
income is one funding option, not a required premise for every purchase. All assumptions must stay
visible when the main narrative is simplified.
A flawless perpetual dollar peg, complete private-key control map and funded external exit are not
established by this evidence. The narrower proposal can be proved conditionally once the missing inputs
and policy are specified.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 174
